My experience with the HV Popular de Botafogo veterinary clinic was very painful and left me with significant questions about their care. My cat, Mia, was treated for respiratory distress, hospitalized, and passed away on October 3, 2026.

After requesting and reviewing her medical records, I found discrepancies in the time of death and the date recorded on the body removal form. The material provided also lacks a detailed sequence of medication administration times, oxygen support, and resuscitation measures, making it difficult to understand the care provided.

I understand that a serious condition can have an unfavorable outcome, but I expected accurate documentation and clear information about everything that happened. I am still seeking clarification from the clinic. Based on this experience, I do not feel confident recommending the establishment.
The doctor was incredibly attentive and caring with the animal, Dr. Aline Lopes! Thank you so much!

They'll charge you 3000 for one night there. They terrorized me, saying my cat might have cancer or lymphoma, that he was dehydrated, etc. They saw I was vulnerable and took advantage of me. They charge cheaply for consultations because they only make money from these unnecessary hospitalizations. I took him to another clinic near Real Grandeza, and I was charged around 400 reais in total with all the exams and a follow-up consultation. If you love your pet, DO NOT take them to this place, they just want to take your money. They should be ashamed of what they do, and then they come and say "veterinarian out of love"

Terrible experience: Lack of hygiene, abusive charges, and my cat remained obstructed.
I arrived at this clinic on Monday at 2 PM (the 10th) with my cat unable to urinate due to obstructive cystitis. The doctor explained that unblocking, catheterization, and irrigation would be necessary for at least 24 hours, requesting a 48-hour hospitalization. I accepted the quote of R$ 3,296.00 because I wanted to save my cat and left my animal there expecting dignified and effective care.
However, the sequence of events was unacceptable:
Deplorable Hygiene Conditions During Hospitalization: On Tuesday, when I went to visit him, I found my cat in a terrible state: quietly in his stall, completely wet with urine, with wet paws and belly, and the carpet completely soaked. I was so shocked that I spent three days crying just remembering finding him in that situation. Everyone who has a cat knows how fundamental hygiene is for feline well-being and health. I had to immediately contact the veterinarian who was treating me to change the rug. Only after the change did my cat feel more dignified enough to be able to lick himself and clean himself from that humiliating situation. At that point, I completely lost confidence in the place, as they should at least have a urine collection bag.

Attempt to Extend Hospitalization and Discharge at the Request of the Pet: On Wednesday morning, after the results of the urine tests from the first day came out, they wanted to request another day of hospitalization. Given everything that happened on Tuesday, I would NEVER leave my animal there any longer. On Wednesday, around 2 pm, I took my cat home by discharge at the request of the pet/against their will, aware that the necessary 48-hour technical procedure should have already been completed, and I took him home.
Immediate Re-obstruction: At home, he ate and tried to follow his routine. However, on Thursday at 6 am, I noticed that he wasn't urinating and was blocked again.

Shock at the Second Clinic: I immediately took him to another veterinary clinic. There, the veterinarian performed another ultrasound, and the professionals expressed profound astonishment upon seeing the amount of sand/sediment and the level of inflammation the cat had when he arrived, requiring further unblocking and flushing for 48 hours. At the second clinic, he underwent the procedures properly, left feeling great, clean, and recovered. The most impressive thing: they charged me less than a third of the price charged by that first clinic.

Exorbitant Prices for a "Popular" Clinic: The place has the word "Popular" prominently displayed on its facade, but charges R$ 882.00 for just 12 applications (6 doses of analgesic and 6 of antibiotic), totaling an absurd R$ 3,296.00 for two days of hospitalization without even the structure to collect the animal's urine.

I am not a veterinarian and I understand that complications can arise for various reasons, but immediately re-obstructing due to excess crystals after the procedures are done is unacceptable. Furthermore, any pet owner knows that leaving a cat urinating on itself in a humid environment does not help the animal's recovery — on the contrary, it only generates stress and risks of infection.

Paying over 3,000 reais at a so-called "popular" clinic to find the animal soaked in its own urine and, worse, still obstructed and full of sediment, is a disgrace. I do not recommend this clinic to anyone. Review your procedures.

The clinic is only focused on profit, with absolutely no empathy for pet owners. The exams are extremely expensive. My cat was spayed 11 days ago, and the stitches were so poorly done that it doesn't even look like Carolina was a veterinary surgeon. The shaving was done so badly that the stitches were placed where there was fur. After 3 days, one stitch broke. I went back to the clinic to see if the veterinarian could prescribe something to help with my cat's stress and prevent more stitches from breaking. The veterinarian, Mateus Marcos CRMV 23077, was initially attentive and said he would prescribe gabapentin to relax her. He also said that my cat would need to be sedated again, the stitches opened, cleaned, and sutured again, which would require 12 hours of hospitalization. Then he quoted me R$1,100.00. I couldn't afford it; I had already spent a huge amount on the spaying. I wanted to go home and see if I could get a card or cash, which would be cheaper. I asked him for the prescription, but when I refused the procedure, HE refused to give it to me. That's when I became extremely upset by the lack of empathy and that it all came down to making more money. MATEUS MARCOS asked me to come downstairs because the girl wanted to talk to me. When I got there to talk to her, a liability waiver came out saying that I was refusing to undergo the procedures and that I had to sign it so that the clinic would be exempt from any responsibility. I ended up arguing with the receptionist Raquel, the clinic manager was sarcastic and didn't want to give me a quote for the procedures. I asked for my cat's medical records, which they refused to give me. Finally, I left the clinic to go to Manguinhos to try to get a free consultation. When I got there, it was closed, it was raining, and my cat was extremely stressed. I went to the pet store and bought a CALMVET herbal medicine based on passionflower (passion fruit), and that's what made my cat stay in absolute rest for 10 days. Thank God my cat is fine, and I will NEVER go back to that clinic. I will send photos of everything later.

I took my cat who was having difficulty defecating, without doing any tests they said he needed to be hospitalized. I've been a pet mom for over 20 years, and I've rescued more than 10 stray animals, I've never seen anything like it.

Then they asked for an X-ray, I said it had to be an ultrasound, I didn't understand why the X-ray.
Then they talked about a blood test + ultrasound that I had suggested.
I said I wouldn't do the tests that day, only the next day (I thought the doctor's conduct and assumptions were terrible, I was going to seek a second opinion), after I said that, she prescribed a laxative and that was it.

I said that my cat needed to be medicated intravenously, because as I had said at the beginning of the consultation he was barely drinking water.

I have never seen such disregard for animal life, thinking only about profit.

I left there and went to another veterinary clinic. The first thing they did was put my cat on an IV drip, gave him dipyrone, mercepton, and vitamins.
They ordered an ultrasound two days after administering the laxative, and said it wasn't a case for hospitalization.
Today, after 24 hours, my cat went to the bathroom and started drinking water normally again.

Don't trust this clinic; they just want to push tests and hospitalization to make a profit.

My cat passed away today after being hospitalized for three days. During that time, several tests were ordered, I bought about 10 medications prescribed by the clinic and paid for all the costs, but unfortunately, there was no conclusive diagnosis.

My feeling was one of extreme frustration. At a time of such pain and fragility, I expected more transparency, care, and commitment to my animal's health. I leave this experience with the impression that there was more concern with performing procedures and expenses than with effectively seeking a proper diagnosis and treatment.

I am sharing my account so that other pet owners are aware of my experience before deciding to take their animals to this clinic.

I took my 16-year-old cat for an evaluation for osteoarthritis, a diagnosis she's had for years, with the goal of having x-rays, ultrasound, and blood tests done.

During the consultation, I felt there was excessive insistence on potential problems and additional tests, without the main investigation being conducted objectively. Several hypotheses of diseases and future procedures were raised, while the main complaint was relegated to the background.

Initially, an x-ray of her lungs was performed, even though my request was related to her leg. During the ultrasound, one of my cat's mammary glands was injured during scraping, causing bleeding. In an attempt to collect blood, multiple unsuccessful punctures were made, resulting in bleeding from her paws and considerable stress for an elderly patient.

What disappointed me most was the lack of follow-up or any contact to find out how she was doing after the procedures. Unfortunately, my experience was negative.
Wonderful service

I absolutely do not recommend this clinic for hospitalization. In short, I would give it MINUS 5 stars. If the consultation is for something simple, it might be okay. But if your pet has a more serious problem, stay away from this clinic. My dog ​​needed hospitalization, and on the fourth day, during visiting hours, I found her frail, alone, curled up in a corner of the "cage" with no one in the ward caring for her. The veterinarian, Aline, was attending to other animals and irresponsibly left those who were hospitalized without any observation. My pet was found alone, with the IV line doubled and the machine beeping, indicating that the medication was not being administered. Neither veterinarian Aline nor another veterinarian who performs imaging exams bothered to see why the machine was beeping or resolve the problem. Total negligence on the part of the clinic, which by law must have at least one assistant 24 hours a day caring for the hospitalized animals. If I witnessed this during visiting hours, I can only imagine what happens at other times or in the middle of the night. The animals are abandoned in the ward, and if they experience any problems, they will die right there, alone, helpless, and without support. They don't CARE for animals out of love. They TREAT them out of love for money.
The final result after a lot of fighting and total loss of trust in this clinic? I warned that I would take my pet to another clinic no matter what. The veterinarian Aline, very arrogantly, said it would be against my will, and I warned that it didn't matter what name they gave it, that my dog ​​wouldn't stay there anymore. So, they ended up discharging her on their own, but incredibly without a definitive diagnosis, even after she had undergone SEVERAL tests and was hospitalized for 4 days, they incredibly couldn't reach a diagnosis. I took her home, and 2 days later I had to hospitalize her in another clinic because all the previous symptoms returned, and I didn't even have a diagnosis to present at the new clinic. Only the tests and what the veterinarian THOUGHT it could be. What I've noticed is that most of the staff are new veterinarians, recently graduated, with little veterinary experience, but arrogant enough to think they know everything. I also started in this profession, but I was humble enough to seek information from more experienced professionals when I wasn't sure about things. I was humble enough to recognize my mistakes and apologize when I was wrong. Leaving a vulnerable animal unattended for hours and then not even taking responsibility or apologizing is a sad attitude. Treating a pet's life cannot be based on "I think," "I believe" it's this or that. Ask for help to reach diagnoses because both animals and their owners need answers when they seek help, they need to be properly welcomed and respected. If a veterinarian is not capable of understanding this, they are in the wrong profession.

My experience was serious, unacceptable, and dangerous. I took my cat for vaccination, and inside the room, four people entered who were unprepared for feline handling (in addition to myself and the veterinarian, the receptionist is a young man who picks up and drops off animals for bathing and grooming), causing extreme panic in the animal and making it impossible to administer the vaccine. I was pressured to pay in cash, under the justification that "it would be cheaper," which directs the consumer to a single form of payment and violates the Consumer Protection Code (article 39 – abusive practice). Even without the vaccine being administered, the clinic stamped the vaccination booklet, which is ethically serious and may constitute a professional infraction according to the rules of the Federal Council of Veterinary Medicine (CFMV), in addition to compromising the veracity of the animal's health history.
Initially, they informed me that the vaccines "would be kept in the refrigerator for me to return another day." When I made it clear that I would not return to the clinic and requested a solution, there was no refund of the amount paid. Instead, they handed me the vaccine vials to take home, even after they had been handled inside the vaccination room. This act is extremely serious and directly violates ANVISA (Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency) and Sanitary Surveillance regulations, which prohibit the delivery of immunobiologicals to the pet owner, require a continuous cold chain, traceability, and rigorous storage control. Vaccines cannot be transported or stored in a domestic environment, which constitutes a sanitary infraction. Furthermore, there was an explicit contradiction: they stated that the vaccines could be stored for future use, but then claimed that they would expire and need to be discarded, which raises serious questions about compliance with good sanitary practices.
During this process, I was mistreated, disrespected, and mocked by the staff.
Since this episode, my cat has shown a permanent change in behavior: he is stressed, hides, runs away, does not trust people, and shows fear even of visitors, evidencing a direct and lasting impact on his emotional well-being.
A very serious report, involving possible sanitary, ethical, and consumer rights violations.
I do not recommend it. I sincerely hope that this "veterinary clinic," which looks more like a pet shop, closes its doors so that no other animal is mistreated the way mine was. Irreversibly.
